## RCA

This kanban task is a re-emission of a finding that was already remediated in
`dab0f0684` on `irad/feature` (3 hours before the kanban task was scheduled).

### Original finding (SIPA assessment ID 35)

```python
# tools/viz/render_png.py:38 (BEFORE fix)
slug = hashlib.sha256(seed.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]
```

The AST capability extractor (`tools/integrity/capability_extractor.py::_CRYPTO_HASHLIB`)
conservatively flags every `hashlib.*` constructor as the `crypto` capability.
No VIZ intake requirement (RTM) authorizes the `crypto` capability, so SIPA
Mode A returns `quarantine` for the `tools` source.

### Fix already applied (commit `dab0f0684` on `irad/feature`)

`fix(viz): replace hashlib.sha256 with zlib.crc32 in render_png slug`
(2026-06-08 18:12:34 EDT, by Sovanna Larry Chuon via Claude Opus 4.8)

```python
# tools/viz/render_png.py:38 (AFTER fix)
slug = format(zlib.crc32(seed.encode("utf-8")) & 0xFFFFFFFF, "08x")
```

The use case is purely a content-addressable slug for filesystem uniqueness,
not a security primitive. `zlib.crc32` is a non-crypto 32-bit hash that SIPA's
detector does not flag (only the `decompress` direction of `zlib/gzip/bz2/lzma`
is flagged under `obfuscation`). The per-second UTC timestamp prefix
(`%Y%m%d_%H%M%S`) already provides uniqueness across separate renders, so
the slug is purely a within-second tiebreaker.

This is the canonical remediation documented in the project memory
[[sipa-hashlib-content-fingerprint-false-positive]]: swap `hashlib.X` for
`format(zlib.crc32(...) & 0xFFFFFFFF, "08x")` for non-security filename
slugs / cache keys. Do not authorize a "crypto" requirement to placate SIPA.

## Why this RCA is a no-op close

The fix `dab0f0684` is already on `irad/feature`. When that branch is
merged to `main`, the SIPA finding will clear automatically. Authoring a
parallel fix on the kanban branch would either:

1. **Cherry-pick `dab0f0684`** — creates a no-op merge conflict with the
   `irad/feature` integration. Wasteful and confusing.
2. **Re-author a different fix** — duplicates the prior memory
   `sipa-hashlib-content-fingerprint-false-positive` and creates
   merge-conflict churn on a hot file.

The right action is to mark this task done with an RCA pointing to the
upstream fix, mirroring the no-op close pattern used by `ci-fix-2723XXXXXX`
tasks earlier this cycle (see `docs/audits/ci-fix-27233157576-rca.md`).
